intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Upgrade to include a silica mud mask and an in-water drink. Visiting in the evening offers a magical experience under the stars and, in winter months, possible northern lights overhead.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic spot offers a more local and intimate geothermal bathing experience at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Settlement Exhibition museum to dive into Norse history.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. This UNESCO World Heritage site offers a once-in-a-lifetime geological experience. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If the skies are clear, step outside briefly to scan for northern lights from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport Keflavik food court or a convenience store snack before shuttle departure - budget around 1,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for real-time northern lights forecasts. Exchange some currency or use a no-fee travel card. January means very limited daylight (roughly 5-6 hours), so plan accordingly. Keep warm layers easily accessible in carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to take in the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. Sunrise is around 11:00 AM in January, so no rush. Pick up groceries at a nearby Bonus or Kronan supermarket (Iceland's most budget-friendly chains) to stock up on breakfast supplies for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort on foot. Visit the nearest coastal cliffs or lava fields for a short introductory hike. Breathe in the fresh Arctic air and photograph the rugged Icelandic landscape. If near Reykjavik, walk along Saebraut coastal road for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Reykjavik (by local bus Strætó, approx. 490 ISK per ride) to explore Laugavegur Street. Window shop and soak in the atmosphere. Check northern lights forecast - if KP index is 3+, head to a dark spot near the coast or Grótta Lighthouse for aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared oats or yogurt from supermarket - budget 500 ISK
meals.lunch: Bonus supermarket sandwich or hot dog from a Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur stand in Reykjavik (the famous Icelandic hot dog) - approx. 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Icelandic submarine sandwiches) or Aktu Taktu burger restaurant for a budget meal - approx. 1,800-2,200 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January daylight is extremely limited. Plan outdoor activities between 11 AM and 3 PM to maximize natural light. The Strætó bus app helps navigate public transport in Reykjavik cheaply.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja Church (exterior is free, tower entry approx. 1,000 ISK). Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik on foot. Stop by the Sun Voyager (Sólfarið) sculpture on the waterfront - completely free and stunning against the winter sky.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik City Library or the free Árbær Open Air Museum (check winter hours). Alternatively, explore the Harpa Concert Hall exterior and waterfront area for free. Walk through the old harbor district and browse the free Kolaportið flea market if open on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunting session. Take a free self-guided tour to Grótta Lighthouse at Seltjarnarnes peninsula (accessible by Strætó bus) - one of Reykjavik's best free aurora viewing spots. Bring thermos with hot cocoa prepared at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort - oatmeal with Skyr (Icelandic yogurt) - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters cafe for soup and bread deal - approx. 1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta or rice dish at resort kitchen if available, or Noodle Station (budget-friendly Asian noodle soup) - approx. 1,600 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Wear wind-proof outer layers at Grótta - coastal winds can be brutal in January. Check aurora forecast at en.vedur.is before heading out. Best aurora viewing is between 10 PM and 2 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Golden Circle (budget option: join a shared tour approx. 7,000-9,000 ISK, or rent a car split between travelers). First stop: Þingvellir National Park - walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Entry to the park is free, parking fee approx. 750 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle: Visit Geysir geothermal area to witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5-10 minutes (free entry). Then head to Gullfoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most dramatic waterfalls, free to visit. Bring crampons or traction devices for icy paths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. If energy permits and skies are clear, set an alarm for midnight northern lights check. The rural drive back may offer excellent aurora views away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Pack sandwiches and snacks from resort before departure - 600 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Geysir or Gullfoss parking area (avoid tourist restaurants which charge 2,500-4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at resort or Bonus supermarket ready meal heated up - 800-1,200 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy in January. Check road conditions at road.is before departure. Dress in multiple warm layers - standing at Gullfoss in January wind is extremely cold. Waterproof boots essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula (accessible by local bus or budget car rental). Explore the Bridge Between Continents - a small footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, free to cross. Walk through dramatic lava fields covered in moss.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon area - while the Blue Lagoon itself is expensive (30,000+ ISK), nearby Reykjanes geothermal area has free hot spring pools. Explore the Gunnuhver mud pools and geothermal vents near Grindavík for free. Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse for coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Visit a local neighborhood geothermal pool (Laugardalslaug or a community hot pot) - these public pools cost only 1,000-1,200 ISK and are where locals actually go. Soak in the hot tubs and steam rooms. Perfect budget alternative to Blue Lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with granola and coffee at resort - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches from resort or Bonus supermarket - 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Reykjavik Fish Market budget option: Icelandic fish and chips from a harbor kiosk - approx. 2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The public swimming pools (sundlaugar) are a cornerstone of Icelandic culture. Locals use them daily. Showering without a swimsuit before entering is mandatory by Icelandic law - follow the signs. This is a genuinely authentic cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Esja Mountain area near Reykjavik. Take a moderate winter hike up Esja (free, parking 500 ISK). The trail to Þverfellshorn viewpoint offers stunning views over Reykjavik and Faxaflói Bay. Only attempt if weather is favorable and you have proper footwear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) - entry approx. 2,500 ISK, covers Iceland's history from settlement to modern times. Alternatively, the Reykjavik City Museum (Landnámssýningin - Settlement Exhibition) has fascinating Viking-age ruins, entry approx. 1,800 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights priority evening. Check forecast at 6 PM. If KP index is favorable, drive or bus to Þingvellir or Hvalfjörður area for dark sky aurora viewing. If skies are cloudy, enjoy a cozy evening at the resort with hot cocoa and plan the next day.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast self-prepared at resort - 500 ISK
meals.lunch: Café Garðurinn vegetarian restaurant offers affordable lunch specials - approx. 1,800 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-cooked lamb soup (kjötsúpa) using ingredients from Bonus - a classic Icelandic comfort dish - approx. 1,000 ISK for ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Esja hike in January requires crampons/ice cleats and trekking poles. Do not attempt in high winds or poor visibility. Always tell someone your hiking plans. The mountain rescue number is 112.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (requires car rental or budget shared tour approx. 9,000-12,000 ISK). Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most photographed spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Snæfellsnes: Visit Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth). Explore Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the dramatic coastal cliffs. Visit Arnarstapi village and walk the free coastal trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey. The drive back along the peninsula offers excellent northern lights opportunities if skies are clear. Stop at a dark pullout point if aurora is visible. Arrive back at resort by 9-10 PM.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from resort before 8 AM departure - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kirkjufell or Djúpalónssandur - 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Grab dinner at a local petrol station grill on the way back (N1 or Orkan stations have surprisingly decent and affordable food) - approx. 1,500-2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is about 2.5 hours from Reykjavik. Road conditions can be challenging in January - check road.is before departure. The peninsula is less crowded than Golden Circle and incredibly dramatic in winter. Fuel up before entering the peninsula as stations are sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and resort relaxation. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Take a beachfront walk near the resort and practice photography of the Icelandic winter coastline. Look for sea birds and seals common along Icelandic shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laugardalur valley in Reykjavik - explore the botanical garden (free in winter), and the Laugardalur geothermal area. Visit Laugardalslaug public pool complex (1,000-1,200 ISK) which has multiple hot tubs, steam room, and a large outdoor geothermal pool. Spend 2-3 hours soaking and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's nightlife area around Austurstræti and Laugavegur. Many bars have happy hours from 5-8 PM with affordable drinks. Alternatively, attend a free or low-cost cultural event - check what's happening at Harpa Concert Hall or local community centers.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at resort - eggs, toast, fruit - 600 ISK
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand (Bill Clinton's favorite!) - two hot dogs for under 1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) - famous for lobster soup at budget prices, approx. 1,800-2,200 ISK. A Reykjavik institution.

day_by_day.notes: The public geothermal pools are the best budget hot spring experience in Iceland. Much cheaper than commercial hot spring spas. Laugardalslaug has excellent facilities including a waterslide and multiple temperature hot pots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip south: Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free, parking 750 ISK) - you can walk behind the waterfall in summer but may be icy/closed in January. Then visit Skógafoss waterfall (free) - climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík - one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks). Entry is free. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves - never turn your back on the ocean. Visit the nearby Reyniskirkja church on the hill.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik. Stop at Seljavallalaug - one of Iceland's oldest swimming pools, a free geothermal pool tucked in a valley (short 15-minute hike in). Bring a towel and swimsuit. Changing facilities are basic. Magical experience especially if aurora appears overhead.

meals.breakfast: Early departure - packed breakfast from resort - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Reynisfjara black beach - 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Stop at Vík village - Suður-Vík restaurant for fish soup or lamb soup - approx. 2,000-2,500 ISK, or pack dinner and eat at resort

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous - sneaker waves have killed tourists. Stay well back from the water and watch the wave patterns before approaching. Seljavallalaug pool is free but the changing room is very basic and cold in January. The pool itself is wonderfully warm.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjavik area hot springs and geothermal sites. Visit Deildartunguhver - Europe's highest-flow hot spring (free to view). Alternatively, visit Hveragerði town (40 min from Reykjavik) known as the geothermal town, where you can hike to natural hot spring rivers in the Reykjadalur valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reykjadalur Hot Spring River hike - a 3km hike (each way) leads to a natural hot river where you can bathe for free. This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The hike takes about 45 minutes each way. Dress warmly as the trail can be icy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. This is a prime northern lights evening - plan to stay up late if forecast is good. Set up near the resort's beachfront for aurora viewing with a warm flask of tea. The coastal location with minimal light pollution can offer excellent aurora sightings.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with granola at resort - 500 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the hike - sandwiches and energy bars - 700 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-cooked Icelandic lamb chops or skyr-marinated chicken from Bonus supermarket - 1,500 ISK for ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Reykjadalur is one of Iceland's best free experiences. The trail can be slippery in January - wear proper footwear. The hot river has designated changing areas. Water temperature varies - test before immersing. This is a locals' favorite and far more authentic than commercial hot spring spas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thor's Valley) if weather and road conditions permit (requires a super-jeep or 4WD - consider a budget shared tour approx. 10,000-13,000 ISK). This dramatic highland valley is surrounded by three glaciers: Eyjafjallajökull, Mýrdalsjökull, and Tindfjallajökull. Alternatively, visit Krýsuvík geothermal area on Reykjanes Peninsula (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: If staying closer to Reykjavik: Visit the Perlan Museum (exterior viewpoint is free, museum entry approx. 2,990 ISK for the Wonders of Iceland exhibition including a real indoor ice cave). The rooftop observation deck offers 360° views over Reykjavik. Explore Öskjuhlíð forest hill surrounding Perlan.
day_by_day.evening: Final major northern lights hunting night. Join a free self-guided aurora chase - drive or bus to Heiðmörk nature reserve on the outskirts of Reykjavik for dark skies. Alternatively, check if any free community aurora viewing events are happening. Photograph the aurora with a smartphone on night mode or a camera on long exposure.

meals.breakfast: Toast with Icelandic butter and jam, coffee - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Thermos soup and packed sandwiches for outdoor adventure - 700 ISK
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Mandi Shawarma (affordable and delicious, popular with locals) or Pylsuvagninn food truck - approx. 1,500-2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Þórsmörk F-roads (mountain roads) are closed in winter and require super-jeep. Only attempt with a proper guided tour. The Perlan ice cave exhibition is worth the splurge if budget allows - it's a unique indoor glacier experience. Aurora forecast check: en.vedur.is

day_by_day.morning: Final full day - revisit your favorite spots or explore anything missed. Consider visiting Elliðaárdalur valley in Reykjavik - a beautiful free nature reserve with a salmon river running through the city. Walk the trails and enjoy Iceland's unique urban-nature interface.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping on a budget: Visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends, 200 ISK entry) for affordable Icelandic souvenirs, second-hand woolens, and local food products. Alternatively, visit Bonus or Krónan supermarket for affordable Icelandic gifts: Skyr, Icelandic sea salt, licorice, Brennivín (Black Death schnapps), and dried fish.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell hot spring soak at Vesturbæjarlaug or Sundhöllin public pool (1,000-1,200 ISK). Reflect on the trip while soaking in geothermal water. Then enjoy a final Reykjavik evening walk along the waterfront. Check aurora one last time - if skies are clear, make the most of your final night.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining groceries from resort - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Icelandic hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur for a classic farewell lunch - 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on farewell dinner at Snaps Bistro Bar or Messinn fish restaurant for authentic Icelandic cuisine - budget 3,500-4,500 ISK as a treat

day_by_day.notes: Budget souvenir tip: Lopapeysa (Icelandic wool sweaters) from flea markets or second-hand shops are much cheaper than tourist boutiques. Dried fish (harðfiskur) and Skyr make excellent and affordable authentic Icelandic gifts. Pack any liquids in checked luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Check-out day. Pack luggage and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on flight time, enjoy a final Icelandic breakfast. Take one last walk along the beachfront. If time permits, visit a nearby geothermal bakery or café for a final Icelandic kleina (twisted doughnut) or skyr cake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport via Flybus (book in advance for best price, approx. 3,000 ISK). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Icelandic spirits or chocolate at airport prices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, dramatic landscapes, and Icelandic culture. The memories of aurora dancing over volcanic landscapes and soaking in geothermal pools will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final self-prepared breakfast at resort using remaining supplies - 400 ISK
meals.lunch: Airport food court or pack remaining snacks for the journey - 1,000-1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Meal on flight or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): Food approx. 35,000-45,000 ISK, Transport approx. 15,000-20,000 ISK, Activities approx. 15,000-20,000 ISK, Total approx. 65,000-85,000 ISK (approx. $450-600 USD). Cooking your own meals at the resort and using public pools instead of commercial spas are the biggest budget savers. The northern lights are free - patience and clear skies are the only requirements!

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a brief moment to step outside and scan the sky for the northern lights if skies are clear — January offers excellent aurora chances.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport convenience store or a quick bite at the resort's late-night offering if available. Stock up on basics at a 24-hour petrol station shop near the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule any daytime activities today. Arrival is at 22:30. Priority is rest after a long flight. Confirm your resort transfer in advance. January sunset is around 16:30 so darkness falls early — ideal aurora conditions if skies cooperate.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's winter atmosphere. The dramatic black lava coastline and crisp Arctic air make for a stunning introduction to the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 10–20 minutes from most southwest Iceland resorts). Pre-book your entry in advance as slots fill quickly. Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Consider the mid-range 'Comfort' package which includes a welcome drink, silica mud mask, and towel. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing and unwinding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head into nearby Reykjavik (about 40–50 minutes by bus or car) for dinner, or dine at a local restaurant near the resort. Afterward, check aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) and if the KP index is favorable, step outside or take a short drive away from light pollution for your first northern lights viewing attempt.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy skyr, Icelandic bread, smoked salmon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Light meal or snack at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant (budget-conscious option: grab a soup and bread at the lagoon's café counter rather than the full restaurant)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkadurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik — mid-range Icelandic cuisine featuring lamb and fish, or try Messinn for excellent pan-fried fish dishes at reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance online — walk-ins are rarely available in January. Bring a waterproof hair tie and avoid putting your hair in the water as the silica can be drying. January daylight hours are roughly 08:00–16:30.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from central Reykjavik. Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic foods including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), rye bread (rúgbrauð), and dried fish (harðfiskur). Visit colorful Hallgrímskirkja church and the historic Aðalstræti area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently after the tour. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) to learn about Iceland's Viking settlement and cultural history — entry around 2,500 ISK. Stroll along Laugavegur shopping street and browse local wool shops, bookstores, and design boutiques. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning glass facade and free interior exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join a small-group guided jeep tour departing from Reykjavik into the Icelandic wilderness, far from city light pollution. Expert guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Dress in your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at Sandholt Bakery in Reykjavik — one of Iceland's best artisan bakeries
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the food walking tour supplement lunch; top up with a bowl of Icelandic lamb soup at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the evening tour at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — a beloved budget-friendly harbor shack famous for its lobster soup and grilled fish skewers

day_by_day.notes: The food walking tour typically lasts 3–4 hours. Book the Northern Lights Jeep tour in advance; reputable operators include Arctic Adventures and Reykjavik Excursions. Most tours offer a free rebooking if aurora activity is too low — confirm this policy when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the iconic Golden Circle route (self-drive or guided day tour). First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk along the Almannagjá rift valley, see the Öxará River, and explore the historic site of Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi). Dramatic winter light makes photography exceptional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Explore the steaming hot spring landscape. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls, especially dramatic with winter ice formations along its edges.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop at Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn on the way back (open until 22:00) for a relaxing soak in natural geothermal pools beside a lake — a quieter, more local alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Enjoy the outdoor steam bath over a natural hot spring vent.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Geysir Center cafeteria or pack a picnic of Icelandic bread, cheese, and smoked lamb purchased from a Bonus supermarket the day before
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn near Fontana — cozy lakeside restaurant serving traditional Icelandic dishes including rye bread baked underground using geothermal heat

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from Reykjavik. Roads in January can be icy — check road conditions at Road.is before departure. A 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Allow 8–10 hours for the full circuit including stops.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast toward Seljalandsfoss waterfall (about 1.5 hours from Reykjavik). In summer you can walk behind it, but in January the path may be icy — admire from the front and nearby viewpoints. Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic, with a staircase climbing to viewpoints above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean. Explore the Reynisfjall basalt cave formations. Visit the picturesque village of Vík.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or hotel in Vík for the night (pre-booked, mid-range option like Hótel Vík í Mýrdal), or drive back toward the resort if preferred. If staying in Vík, enjoy dinner locally and scan the skies for northern lights from this darker, rural location — excellent aurora viewing potential away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Skál! Eatery in Skógar near Skógafoss — hearty Icelandic lamb soup and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — cozy local restaurant with traditional Icelandic fish and lamb dishes at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: South Coast roads are generally well-maintained but can be slippery in January. Skógafoss steps may be icy — use traction cleats (microspikes) which can be rented or purchased in Reykjavik. Check weather forecasts carefully. Daylight is limited so start early.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighting near Vík, drive east to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 2.5 hours). This otherworldly lagoon is filled with enormous blue icebergs calving from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. Take a short walk around the lagoon shore. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating surreal ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 200 meters to Diamond Beach — where translucent icebergs wash ashore on a black sand beach, glittering like diamonds in the low winter sun. Spend time photographing this magical landscape. Visit the nearby Fjallsárlón glacier lagoon for a quieter, equally stunning alternative. Begin the drive back westward.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir on the return journey (open until 22:00, approximately 100 km from Reykjavik). Soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool — a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Surrounded by steaming geothermal vents and a small geyser, this is a more intimate and authentic experience than the Blue Lagoon. Return to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Vík or packed breakfast from a petrol station
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Visitor Center café — soup, sandwiches, and hot drinks (essential for warming up)
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort restaurant or a quick stop at a local restaurant in Selfoss on the return drive — try Tryggvaskáli for Icelandic comfort food

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 375 km from Reykjavik — this is a long driving day (5+ hours total driving). Start very early. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir costs around 3,200 ISK per adult. Pre-book online. Road conditions between Vík and Jökulsárlón can be challenging in January — check Road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Take advantage of any on-site spa or hot tub facilities. Stroll along the beachfront and enjoy the dramatic winter seascape. Use the morning to review photos, plan remaining days, and recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Reykjavik for a relaxed afternoon of independent exploration. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) featuring Icelandic modern art — affordable entry around 1,800 ISK. Explore the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends — if applicable) or browse the boutiques along Skólavörðustígur street. Visit the famous Sun Voyager (Sólfar) sculpture by the harbor waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a proper mid-range dinner in Reykjavik followed by a cultural evening. Check if any concerts are playing at Harpa Concert Hall. Return to the resort and keep aurora alerts active on your phone — clear January nights offer the best viewing chances of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Cozy café lunch at Stofan Café in Reykjavik — homemade soups, sandwiches, and excellent coffee in a vintage living-room atmosphere
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic seafood in a mid-range setting, excellent value tasting options available

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day — Iceland's winter conditions and long driving days are physically demanding. Use this day to launder clothes, restock supplies at Bónus supermarket (Iceland's most budget-friendly grocery chain), and reorganize gear.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. Join a guided snorkeling tour between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial meltwater with visibility exceeding 100 meters. The water is 2–4°C year-round but dry suits keep you warm. This is a once-in-a-lifetime geological experience. Tours typically depart 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate provided by your tour guide. Explore more of Þingvellir National Park on foot — walk the Hakið viewpoint trail for panoramic views over the rift valley and Lake Þingvallavatn. Visit the church (Þingvallakirkja) and the historic Law Rock (Lögberg). The low winter sun creates golden-hour light for most of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Book a second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep if the first attempt on Day 3 was clouded out, or simply monitor conditions independently. If skies are clear, drive 10–15 minutes from the resort to a dark spot and watch for the aurora. Pack a thermos of hot tea and warm blankets.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the Silfra tour — essential fuel for a cold-water experience
meals.lunch: Pack a warm lunch in a thermos — the Silfra area has no nearby restaurants; alternatively, stop at the Þingvellir Visitor Center café
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a local restaurant near the resort or in Reykjavik — try Hamborgarabúllan for Iceland's best gourmet burgers at a mid-range price point

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires you to be a confident swimmer. Minimum age is typically 12 years. Book well in advance with operators like DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures. Dry suit rental is included. Do not drink alcohol before snorkeling. Water temperature is 2–4°C — the dry suit keeps your body warm but face and hands will feel the cold.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula — the volcanic landscape surrounding your resort area. Visit the Bridge Between Continents, a small footbridge spanning a rift between the tectonic plates. Explore the Reykjanesviti lighthouse, Iceland's oldest, perched on dramatic lava cliffs. Walk through the Gunnuhver geothermal area with its powerful mud pools and steam vents — Iceland's largest hot spring area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Eldheimar Museum in Heimaey on Vestmannaeyjar (Westman Islands) — if a day ferry is feasible — or alternatively explore the Reykjanes area further with a visit to Kleifarvatn lake, a mysterious and hauntingly beautiful volcanic lake surrounded by lava fields and steaming vents. Walk the lakeshore trail for striking winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Treat yourself to a soak in the resort's hot tub or pool if available. Enjoy dinner at the resort restaurant tonight — a mid-trip treat without the need to drive. Review your aurora forecast and step outside periodically to check the sky.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a petrol station diner in Grindavík — Grindavík has a few local cafés serving fish and chips and Icelandic staples
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — enjoy a proper sit-down dinner featuring local Icelandic ingredients; budget approximately 4,000–6,000 ISK per person for a two-course meal

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly geothermally active and volcanic. As of recent years, volcanic activity in this region has been ongoing — check current safety advisories and road closures before visiting. The area around Grindavík may have restricted access. Always follow official guidance from Almannavarnir (Civil Protection).

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided or self-drive excursion to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort). Visit the iconic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano — the setting of Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Explore Arnarstapi village with its dramatic basalt arch formations and birdcliff coastline. Walk the coastal path to Hellnar village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its eerie lava formations and the remains of a shipwreck. Stop at Kirkjufell mountain — one of Iceland's most photographed peaks — and the nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall. The mountain is particularly dramatic against a winter sky.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward the resort. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is an excellent aurora viewing location due to minimal light pollution. If conditions are favorable (check Vedur.is aurora forecast), pull over at a dark viewpoint along the peninsula for aurora watching before heading home. Return to resort by 22:00–23:00.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar — a beloved cliffside café serving homemade soup, cakes, and coffee with stunning ocean views; a true Icelandic gem
meals.dinner: Hotel Búðir restaurant (if budget allows for a splurge) — one of Iceland's finest dining experiences in a remote setting, or pack a hearty dinner to eat on the road

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day excursion — approximately 5–6 hours driving total plus stops. Start no later than 08:30. Mountain roads on the peninsula can be closed in severe winter weather — check road.is. A 4WD vehicle is essential. Fuel up before leaving the Reykjavik/Borgarnes area as petrol stations are sparse on the peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir if not visited on Day 6, or revisit for a longer, more leisurely soak. Alternatively, explore the Kerið volcanic crater lake — a stunning red and ochre crater filled with a vivid turquoise lake, just 15 minutes from Selfoss. Walk the crater rim for panoramic views. Entry is approximately 800 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Selfoss — Iceland's largest town outside the capital area. Browse local shops, visit the farmers market if operating, and enjoy a relaxed afternoon pace. Drive to Hveragerði — a geothermal town famous for its greenhouses and the Reykjadalur hot spring river. The hike to the hot river is approximately 3 km each way (45–60 minutes) and rewards with a natural river you can bathe in.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for your penultimate full evening. Enjoy a special dinner in Reykjavik to celebrate the near-end of your trip. If aurora activity has been elusive, book a final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep for tonight — January is peak aurora season and guides are highly motivated to find clear skies.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Geysir Glima in Hveragerði — a local bakery and café serving fresh pastries, sandwiches, and Icelandic treats
meals.dinner: Apotek Kitchen & Bar in Reykjavik — stylish mid-range restaurant in a historic pharmacy building, excellent cocktails and Icelandic-inspired dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot river hike is approximately 6 km round trip with moderate elevation gain. Trails can be icy in January — wear microspikes and bring a change of clothes for bathing. Water temperature in the river varies — wade in gradually and find your ideal spot. Changing facilities are minimal; bring a large towel.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort and take a long, reflective walk along the beachfront. Revisit any favorite spots near the resort. Pack souvenirs and gifts purchased throughout the trip. Visit the Keflavik area's Duus Museum if interested in local maritime heritage and Icelandic art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for final souvenir shopping along Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur. Must-buy Icelandic souvenirs include lopapeysa (traditional wool sweaters) from the Handknitting Association of Iceland, Icelandic sea salt, skyr, and locally designed ceramics. Visit the Kolaportið flea market if it's a weekend. Take a final stroll around the old harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik — splurge slightly on a memorable final meal. Afterward, take a final aurora watch attempt. Head to Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) just above Reykjavik for a slightly elevated, less light-polluted viewpoint within the city, or drive 15 minutes out of town for darker skies. Return to the resort for final packing.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — savor your last Icelandic skyr and smoked salmon spread
meals.lunch: Braud & Co bakery in Reykjavik — Iceland's most beloved artisan bakery, famous for its cinnamon rolls and sourdough; casual and affordable
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur — one of Reykjavik's most celebrated restaurants specializing in traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique; a worthy farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: Complete all souvenir shopping today — airport shops are significantly more expensive. Confirm your departure transfer or car return logistics for tomorrow. Set an early alarm. Pack your bags tonight and set aside any liquids or restricted items for carry-on compliance.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early for final preparations. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort — savor your final cup of Icelandic coffee. Check out and arrange transfer or drive to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 20–45 minutes from most southwest Iceland locations). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Browse the duty-free shops for last-minute Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolate, and skincare products (Skyn Iceland). Reflect on 13 incredible days of geothermal wonders, dramatic landscapes, and the magic of the northern lights.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — check-out may allow an early breakfast; confirm timing with the resort
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavik — Fljótt og Gott (Quick and Good) offers affordable Icelandic lamb soup and sandwiches airside
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at home destination

day_by_day.notes: Keflavik Airport is approximately 50 km from Reykjavik and 20–30 km from most Reykjanes Peninsula accommodations. Flybus and Airport Express coaches run regularly from Reykjavik BSÍ terminal. If self-driving, return the rental car at the airport and allow 30 extra minutes for the return process. Iceland's VAT refund (up to 15%) can be claimed at the airport for purchases over 6,000 ISK — keep your receipts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Upgrade to include a silica mud mask and an in-water drink. Visiting in the evening offers a magical experience under the stars and, in winter months, possible northern lights overhead.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic spot offers a more local and intimate geothermal bathing experience at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Settlement Exhibition museum to dive into Norse history.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. This UNESCO World Heritage site offers a once-in-a-lifetime geological experience. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink, and settle into your beachfront suite. If skies are clear, step outside briefly — the resort's coastal darkness makes it a surprisingly good spot for a first glimpse of the Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín) arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort to pre-stock your suite with Icelandic snacks, sparkling water, and a bottle of local craft beer or Icelandic gin as a welcome amenity. Confirm Northern Lights alert service with the concierge tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape. Breathe in the Arctic air and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-famous Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, just a short drive from the resort. Book the premium Retreat Spa package, which includes exclusive access to the private lagoon, in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a multi-course meal at the Retreat Restaurant. Spend 3–4 luxurious hours soaking in the milky-blue 38–40°C geothermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort refreshed. Enjoy a fine dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), head to the resort's private terrace or beach for your first dedicated Northern Lights viewing session. The KP index forecast should be checked with the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast at the resort — skyr parfait, smoked lamb, fresh-baked rye bread, and Icelandic butter
meals.lunch: Multi-course Retreat Restaurant meal included in the Blue Lagoon Retreat package — expect langoustine bisque, Arctic char, and lava-chocolate dessert
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — pan-seared cod with dill beurre blanc, reindeer tenderloin, and Icelandic moss-infused cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa well in advance as it sells out quickly. January is peak Northern Lights season — KP index of 2 or above is sufficient at Iceland's latitude. Ask the concierge to set up an aurora alert on your phone.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula's volcanic landscape by luxury 4WD. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (where Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools, and the dramatic Reykjanesviti lighthouse — Iceland's oldest. A private geologist guide explains the raw volcanic forces shaping this UNESCO Global Geopark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. Don a dry suit and descend into one of the world's clearest bodies of water, with visibility exceeding 100 meters. Float between two tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water filtered through lava rock for decades. A premium small-group experience with expert dive guides.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik for dinner at one of Iceland's most celebrated fine dining establishments — Dill Restaurant (New Nordic cuisine, Michelin-starred) or Óx (intimate 12-seat chef's table). Afterward, private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Icelandic waffles with crowberry jam, smoked salmon, and Skyr
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch provided by the resort for the Silfra excursion — smoked lamb wraps, Icelandic cheese, thermos of hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant or Óx — tasting menu featuring foraged Icelandic ingredients, Arctic herbs, and locally sourced proteins paired with Icelandic craft beers or wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Silfra water is approximately 2°C year-round — dry suits are provided but fingers and face will feel the cold. Minimum certification required for diving; snorkeling requires no certification. Book Dill or Óx reservation weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour with a premium private guide. Explore the colorful streets of Iceland's capital, visiting the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the Harpa Concert Hall, and hidden Viking-age archaeological sites. Sample traditional Icelandic street food including pylsur (hot dogs with all toppings), skyr cheesecake, and fermented shark (hákarl) for the adventurous.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland and the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) for deep Viking heritage immersion. Then explore the upscale Laugavegur shopping street for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), luxury design items, and artisan souvenirs. Stop at Kaffitár or Reykjavik Roasters for Iceland's finest specialty coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join a small-group guided jeep tour departing from Reykjavik into the dark Icelandic wilderness. Expert aurora guides use real-time weather and KP-index data to position the group for optimal viewing. Hot cocoa and Icelandic pastries served under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked Arctic char eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed Icelandic berry juice
meals.lunch: During the Food & Culture Tour — curated tastings across multiple Reykjavik eateries including Grillmarkaðurinn for gourmet Icelandic tapas
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur — traditional Icelandic cuisine reimagined (salted cod head, lamb soup, skyr mousse) before the Northern Lights tour

day_by_day.notes: Dress in extreme warmth for the Northern Lights jeep tour — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below. The jeep tour typically runs 3–4 hours and covers 50–150 km depending on aurora activity. January offers up to 18 hours of darkness, maximizing aurora viewing windows.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes Peninsula's volcanic craters, lava fields, and steaming fissures. Aerial views of the Blue Lagoon from above, the Fagradalsfjall volcano area, and the dramatic coastline. Land at a remote location for a champagne toast on the lava field.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak at Flúðir — a 90-minute drive into the Icelandic countryside. Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool (dating to 1891) surrounded by geysers and hot spring activity. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this is an authentic, intimate geothermal experience with naturally heated 38–40°C spring water.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the resort with a private chef's table experience arranged by the concierge — a curated 6-course tasting menu of Icelandic seasonal ingredients prepared tableside. Pair with an Icelandic wine and spirits flight. Post-dinner aurora watch from the private beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before helicopter departure — Icelandic pastries, skyr, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch in the Secret Lagoon area — Flúðir village café for homemade lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Private 6-course chef's table at the resort — langoustine carpaccio, reindeer consommé, pan-seared halibut, Arctic berry sorbet, and Icelandic cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent. Have a backup activity ready (additional spa time or cultural visit). The Secret Lagoon is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Golden Circle — private luxury vehicle and guide. Begin at Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) for a morning walk through the rift valley where Iceland's first parliament convened in 930 AD. Dramatic January light creates extraordinary photographic conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle with the explosive Geysir geothermal field — witness Strokkur erupting every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–40 meters into the frigid air. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January, creating an otherworldly ice sculpture landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Friðheimar — a unique restaurant inside a geothermal greenhouse where tomatoes are grown year-round using Iceland's natural heat. The entire menu is tomato-based, from cocktails to dessert, in a magical candlelit greenhouse setting. Return to resort for aurora watching.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs from Icelandic free-range hens, smoked lamb hash, rye bread with crowberry butter
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by the resort for the Golden Circle — thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant — tomato bisque, burrata with heirloom tomatoes, slow-roasted lamb with tomato reduction, tomato sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Roads around the Golden Circle are generally well-maintained but a 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended in January. Sunrise in Iceland in mid-January is around 11:00 AM and sunset around 4:00 PM — plan photo stops accordingly for the magical golden-hour light.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxation and wellness morning at the resort. Enjoy a private hot stone massage and geothermal facial at the resort spa, designed to rejuvenate after a week of adventuring. Spend time in the resort's private hot tub overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ice cave exploration tour — a private guided excursion to a natural glacier ice cave (likely at Langjökull or Mýrdalsjökull glacier, accessible as a day trip). Walk through electric-blue ice tunnels formed by centuries of glacial compression. A certified glacier guide leads the experience with all safety equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second attempt/dedicated session) — depart at optimal forecast time based on KP index. Tonight's session includes a private guide and a custom aurora photography workshop to capture the lights with your camera or smartphone. Hot chocolate and Icelandic cinnamon rolls served in the field.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast in bed — smoked salmon bagel, fresh berries, and Icelandic coffee delivered to your suite
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the resort — Icelandic seaweed salad, poached Arctic char, and elderflower spritz
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at the resort — quick but elegant: Icelandic lamb burger with truffle fries and a craft IPA from Ölvisholt Brugghús brewery

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are only available in winter (November–March) and must be booked with certified glacier guides. Wear waterproof boots and warm layers. The ice cave interiors are a constant 0°C. This is one of Iceland's most photogenic experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile adventure on Langjökull glacier — Iceland's second-largest glacier. A private transfer takes you to the glacier base where you suit up in full snowmobile gear. Race across the vast white expanse with panoramic views of the Icelandic highlands. Optional: visit the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Decompression afternoon — return to the resort and spend time in the private outdoor geothermal pool (if available at resort) or return to the Blue Lagoon for a second, more leisurely soak. This time, book an in-water floating massage and the algae body scrub treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 4:30 PM) cocktail hour at the resort bar — sip an Icelandic gin and tonic with Arctic thyme while watching the brief but spectacular winter twilight over the ocean. Dinner at the resort followed by a private stargazing and aurora session on the private beach with a telescope provided by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast before snowmobiling — Icelandic oatmeal with bilberries, scrambled eggs, thick-cut bacon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at the glacier base camp — hearty lamb stew, fresh bread, and hot coffee
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — slow-braised short rib with Icelandic root vegetables, truffle mashed potato, and a dessert of skyr panna cotta with crowberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobiling requires a valid driver's license. Minimum age is typically 18 to drive solo. Children can ride as passengers. The glacier excursion is weather-dependent — have a backup indoor activity planned.

day_by_day.morning: Private whale watching boat tour from Reykjavik Old Harbour — January is a quieter month but humpback whales and minke whales are occasionally spotted. The tour uses a premium vessel with heated cabins, and expert marine biologists narrate the journey. Even if whales are elusive, the dramatic winter seascape and birdlife are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik Art Museum and the Árbær Open Air Museum — a living history museum showcasing traditional Icelandic turf houses and farm life. Then visit the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland) with its spectacular 360° observation deck and the indoor ice cave exhibit — a perfect complement to real ice cave experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Premium dinner at Geysir Bistro or Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for the legendary langoustine soup — a Reykjavik institution. Then enjoy a performance at Harpa Concert Hall (check January schedule for the Iceland Symphony Orchestra or cultural events). Private transfer back to resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with whipped cream and jam, smoked trout, and fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Lækjarbrekka restaurant in Reykjavik — traditional Icelandic cuisine in a historic 19th-century house; try the puffin or minke whale (sustainably sourced) for an authentic experience
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn for legendary lobster (langoustine) soup as a starter, followed by a reservation at Apotek Kitchen & Bar for the main event — creative Nordic cuisine in a stunning apothecary-themed setting

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January has lower success rates than summer but the experience is still extraordinary. Choose an operator that offers a free repeat trip guarantee if no whales are sighted. Check Harpa's concert schedule well in advance and book tickets early.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day South Coast adventure — private luxury 4WD tour. Begin with the stunning Seljalandsfoss waterfall (walkable behind the falls in summer, but spectacular even in winter ice form). Then continue to Skógafoss waterfall with its famous rainbow mist and Viking legend of hidden treasure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Iceland's South Coast to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic surf. Visit the picturesque fishing village of Vík í Mýrdal. Optional: stop at the Sólheimajökull glacier tongue for a guided glacier walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey with a stop at a remote countryside restaurant or a farm-to-table dinner experience. Arrive back at the resort in time for a final aurora watch from the private beach — by now you'll be a seasoned aurora spotter.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — packed efficiently for an early departure; smoked salmon bagel and coffee in a thermal flask
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — panoramic ocean views, Icelandic fish and chips, lamb burger, and local craft beer
meals.dinner: Rauða Húsið (The Red House) in Eyrarbakki on the return route — one of Iceland's most beloved rural restaurants; try the lobster tails and Icelandic lamb rack

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast road (Route 1/Ring Road) is generally accessible in winter but can close due to blizzards. Always check road.is before departure. Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the waterline.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury horseback riding on Icelandic horses — a private guided ride through the volcanic lava fields and coastal landscape near the resort. Icelandic horses are uniquely gaited (the tölt) and are exceptionally sure-footed on rough terrain. Ride through steaming geothermal vents for a surreal winter landscape experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Art Museum and the Viking World Museum (Víkingaheimar) in Njarðvík — home to a full-scale replica of a Viking ship (Íslendingur) that sailed to America. Explore exhibits on Norse navigation, mythology, and Icelandic settlement history.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (third session) — on a clear night, this is your best chance for a prolonged aurora display as you've now learned the best local spots. Request a private jeep tour for just your group. Pair with a thermos of Brennivín schnapps and a blanket under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — hearty before the horseback ride; Icelandic porridge (hafragrautur) with brown sugar and cream, plus a full cooked breakfast
meals.lunch: Post-riding warm lunch at the stables or a nearby café — lamb soup and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Slippurinn restaurant (if a day trip to Westman Islands is feasible) or back at the resort — Icelandic lamb chops with wild herb crust, roasted root vegetables, and a glass of Icelandic birch wine

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic horses are gentle and suitable for all riding abilities. No experience necessary. Helmets and riding gear are provided. The Viking World Museum is a hidden gem often skipped by tourists — highly recommended for history enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private geothermal spa day — book a private session at one of Iceland's luxury off-the-beaten-path geothermal pools such as Sky Lagoon (Reykjavik's newest premium geothermal spa with a stunning oceanfront infinity edge). Enjoy the 7-step Skjól ritual: warm lagoon, cold plunge, sauna, steam room, cold mist, scrub, and warm lagoon again.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Reykjavik exploration — visit the Hallgrímskirkja church tower for panoramic city views, browse the Kolaportið flea market (Saturdays/Sundays only — adjust if needed), and pick up final luxury souvenirs: Icelandic wool goods, lava jewelry, Icelandic sea salt, and artisan schnapps. Visit the Icelandic Handknitting Association store for authentic lopapeysa sweaters.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's most prestigious restaurants — book a private dining room at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) for a theatrical fire-and-ice dining experience featuring Icelandic prime cuts cooked on a lava stone grill. Toast the journey with Icelandic sparkling birch water and a premium wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — celebratory final morning spread; smoked salmon, caviar blini, Icelandic cheeses, fresh pastries, and champagne
meals.lunch: Sky Lagoon's Gelmir Lagoon Bar — sip a cocktail while soaking; light bites of Icelandic flatbread with smoked fish
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn — dry-aged Icelandic beef, lobster tail, reindeer carpaccio, and a lava-chocolate fondant dessert; full wine pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Sky Lagoon is located just 7 minutes from central Reykjavik and offers a more intimate, design-forward experience than the Blue Lagoon. Book the Pure Pass or Skjól Pass for the full ritual experience. This is an ideal penultimate evening — relaxed yet celebratory.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beachfront (sunrise around 11:00 AM in January, so enjoy a slow morning). Pack, check out, and store luggage with the concierge. Take a final dip in any available resort hot tub or outdoor geothermal pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time: if afternoon departure, head directly to Keflavik Airport (45-minute drive from Reykjavik area) via private luxury transfer. If time allows, stop at the Blue Lagoon one final time for a farewell soak — it is conveniently located en route to the airport. The Blue Lagoon offers luggage storage and shower facilities, making it a perfect pre-flight stop.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Relax in the Saga Lounge (available with Business Class tickets or Priority Pass) with Icelandic snacks and a final glass of Brennivín or Icelandic craft beer before your flight. Carry home memories of dancing auroras, steaming lagoons, and the raw beauty of the land of fire and ice.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast — order everything you loved over the past 13 days; a true Icelandic farewell spread
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (if stopping en route to airport) — smoked lamb flatbread and langoustine soup
meals.dinner: Airport Saga Lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer the night before. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Keflavik. The Blue Lagoon en-route stop requires advance booking even for a brief visit. Tip generously for outstanding guides and resort staff who made the trip exceptional.
